svg.data-zr-capacity: up to 8x 400G ZR in either airflow orientation, or up to 6 in total if any OpenZR+ is mixed in; ZR/OpenZR+ modules must not sit in adjacent ports (HIG Port Overview, Figures 12 and 13)
svg.data-oob: 1x RJ45 100/1000M plus 2x SFP+ 10G, both reaching the x86 (HIG section 12)
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A; MTCTE

The back-to-front build (blue handles and latches, FAN-405637-CD) is orderable and is not modelled; no held document ties a PSU part number to a latch colour (see the psu-airflow-sku-mapping gap) and none prints a chassis SKU (see chassis-sku)","kind":"base"},"dc":{"bays":{"psu-0":"ufispace/psu-132-dc@1","psu-1":"ufispace/psu-132-dc@1"},"description":"Dual 1300W DC PSUs (-40 to -75 V, screw-terminal input) with front-to-back airflow fans; the HIG's rear elevation on page 13 is this build","kind":"orderable"}},"datasheet":{"title":"UfiSpace S9301-32D 400G Data Center Switch Datasheet","url":"https://www.ufispace.com/products/datacenter/400g/s9301-32d-400g-data-center-spine-switch"},"description":"UfiSpace S9301-32D 400G data center spine switch - 1RU white box, 32x QSFP-DD 400G in two belly-to-belly rows plus a 2x2 SFP+ block (a 10G out-of-band pair and the vendor's numbered 1/10G MGMT pair), Broadcom Tomahawk 3 at 12.8 Tbps; six hot-swap fans (5+1) and dual 1300W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable in AC or DC and in front-to-back or back-to-front airflow","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"The HIG's section 10 tables the five system lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the RJ45 management jack, and says nothing about the port lamps. WHICH port each strip column serves is NOT a gap on this device - Figure 11 prints the port number over each lamp column, so the mapping in this manifest is transcribed, not inferred - but what the four lamps in a column MEAN is unstated: not whether they are four 100G lanes of a 400G port, not link against activity, and not what the SFP+ lamp beside each up/down arrow signals. Every port lamp therefore keeps the component's off/on default rather than an invented vocabulary.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfpdd-400g","sfp-plus-oob","sfp-plus-mgmt","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"Measured on THIS device's rear elevation at 5x (see the fan-face provenance): the fan grille face is 43.5 mm wide - matching the HIG component table's 43.4 x 100 x 40 mm - and the airflow tag, captive screw and status lamp sit on a 7.1 mm CHASSIS web between bays, together making the 51.06 mm repeat. The shared ufispace/fan-405637@1 contract draws that flange as part of a 50.7 mm module face, citing the S9110-32X's Figure 15 for putting the tag and screw on the module. Both readings cannot be right and this one was taken from this device's own figure rather than copied from the sibling S9300-32D's identically-named gap, which records the same conflict from the other side (it concluded 43.4 measures the body behind the face). The manifest seats the 50.7 mm component so the bays are not left with a part that overflows them.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/fan-405637@1","fans"],"wanted":"a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-405637, or a caliper on the FRU and the web","what":"fan-faceplate-width"},{"note":"The two END lane-LED strips are half the width of the seven interior ones - one lamp column, not two - which is what makes nine strips serve thirty-two ports and is confirmed twice: Figure 11 prints a single port number over each ('0'/'1' and '30'/'31') where the interior strips print two, and the front photograph puts a single blue column at 70.8 and 427.9 mm. The library holds only the two-column ufispace/qsfpdd-led-strip-2x4@1 and this device may not add components, so both ends seat the wide part and its bezel overhangs the real metal by 2.8 mm outboard. This is a MODELLING compromise that the matched-scale comparison makes visible, not a doubt about the hardware.","reason":"needs-hardware","scope":["port-leds","qsfpdd-400g"],"wanted":"a single-column ufispace/qsfpdd-led-strip-1x4 component","what":"end-led-strip-width"},{"note":"The datasheet lists four AC/DC PSU SKUs by airflow word (PSU-132-AESR 'exhaust air flow', -AISB 'intake air flow', and the DC pair the same way) and the HIG's Figures 6 and 8 distinguish the two builds only by LATCH COLOUR ('blue latch' for back-to-front, 'red latch' for front-to-back). No held document joins a part number to a colour or to a system airflow direction, so the configurations here name the airflow and let the PSU components keep their own model attrs rather than asserting a pairing. The fan side IS documented by colour (HIG Fan Overview: blue handle back-to-front, red handle front-to-back) and the red FAN-405637-HD is what the modelled build seats.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["psus","ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide that prints the SKU beside the airflow direction","what":"psu-airflow-sku-mapping"},{"note":"The HIG port table numbers the MGMT SFP+ pair 0~1 and Figure 11 prints a large white '0' and '1', but it prints them on the highlighted module faces inside the cages - where a seated transceiver would cover them - exactly as it prints the QSFP-DD numbers on the module faces. The QSFP-DD numbers turn out to be printed on the LED strips instead; no held image resolves where, or whether, the SFP+ pair's numbers are printed on the metal, so none are drawn.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["sfp-plus-mgmt"],"wanted":"a close-up photograph of the SFP+ block on a real unit","what":"mgmt-port-numerals"},{"note":"No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name only S9301-32D, and the Available to Order section names only the PSUs and fans. Per the S9510-28DC precedent in this library (whose SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no PDF), orderable SKUs for the AC/DC and airflow builds exist somewhere; the configurations therefore carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs","what":"chassis-sku"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"5+1","redundancy-note":"5+1 - 5+1 hot-swappable (attrs fan-redundancy)"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster at the left edge of the face - the RS-232 console RJ45, the USB 3.0 service port, the out-of-band RJ45 and the recessed reset button, which the HIG Figure 5 callout list treats as one block","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to particular ports - the eighteen blue QSFP-DD lane strips, the four SFP+ lamps and the OOB RJ45's two integrated lamps","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 hot-swappable active-active"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfpdd-400g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus-mgmt":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"description":"the right stacked SFP+ pair under the orange MGMT band, the vendor's ports 0-1, usable as Ethernet or in-band management (HIG 'Connecting the Management Cables'; the datasheet and the HIG port table call them 1/10G)","index-origin":0,"role":"management","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus-oob":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"description":"the left stacked SFP+ pair, marked with the network symbol - the second out-of-band path to the x86 (HIG 'Connecting the OOB Management Cables')","index-origin":0,"role":"management","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the chassis indicators - SYS, FAN, PSU0, PSU1 and the blue ID beacon","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9301-32D","name":"s9301-32d","portfolio":{"family":"Data Center Switch","line":"Cloud & Data Centers"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"attrs":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Physical, Performance, Environmental and Regulatory Compliance sections plus the Available to Order lists, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim and semicolon-separated, untidied; note that MTCTE appears in the datasheet under both EMC and Environment and is carried in both."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 1RU, 436 x 645 x 43.8 mm', weight 11.34 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple (17.17\" x 25.4\" x 1.72\"). 436 is the body between the ear planes, not a rack face: the HIG Space Clearance section says the S9301-32D 'width is 17.17 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', so the mounting hardware is additional to 436 and is not drawn. Depth 645 is the chassis without FRUs; the same section adds 25 mm for the fan handles and 38 mm for the PSU handles beyond it."},"fan-face":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured, AND IT DISAGREES WITH THE SHARED COMPONENT. At 5x zoom on the 600 dpi rear elevation, fan 0's grille face runs x 13.77-57.3 (43.5 mm, which is the HIG component table's 43.4 mm fan module width to within the figure's resolution) and is followed by a 7.1 mm CHASSIS web carrying the 'FAN (arrow) 0' legend, the red 'E' airflow tag, the captive thumbscrew and the fan status lamp, before fan 1's face begins at 64.4. The library's ufispace/fan-405637@1 draws that flange as part of the 50.7 mm module face instead. The bays here are 50.7 mm on the measured 51.06 mm pitch so the existing component seats without overflowing, and the disagreement is registered as a gap rather than papered over; the FAN legends are consequently drawn above the bays at y 1.9 rather than at their measured y 4.7-10.1, where the module would paint over them."},"front-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - HIG Figure 11 at 8.025 px/mm, measured on the 600 dpi page render, with positions good to about 0.3 mm along x. Left to right: a management cluster at the left edge (reset pinhole, five system lamps beside a printed white legend block, a vent field below, and a silver-plated vertical stack of console RJ45 / USB 3.0 / OOB RJ45), then the 2x2 SFP+ block in two silver ganged shells, then the 32 QSFP-DD in eight 2x2 groups separated by blue lane-LED strips. Silver plate behind the jack stack measured at x 14.83-30.78, y 6.42-38.26; the three library apertures composed into it (std/rj45-ganged 12.7 x 11.0, std/usb-a 12.0 x 4.5) match the drawn openings (12.4 x 10.6 and 12.6 x 5.7) far better than the 15.8 x 13.2 single-port housings (std/rj45@2) would: two of those plus the 4.5 mm-tall USB opening stack to 30.9 mm, leaving under 1 mm of the 31.8 mm plate's height for any gap between them, against 5.3 mm of room with the 12.7 x 11.0 cells actually used."},"front-vertical":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing/photo - THE ONE NUMBER ON THIS FACE THAT FOUR SOURCES HAD TO AGREE ON. The port block is mirror-symmetric about y 22.8, and the two cage rows sit on a 14.5 mm pitch with their openings centred at y 15.55 and 30.05. That came from four readings which spread over +/-0.6 mm and were taken independently: (a) the HIG figure's light-grey cage assembly spans y 9.0-34.9 at four different x positions, centre 21.95; (b) the blue LED strips span 7.68-21.02 and 25.05-38.39, centre 23.04; (c) the SFP+ ganged frames span 10.8-20.9 and 25.3-34.9, centre 22.85, pitch 14.25; (d) the front PHOTOGRAPH's dark cage apertures sit at 11.5-19.3 and 26.2-34.0, centre 22.75, pitch 14.7. Reading (b) alone would have given a 17.37 mm row pitch, which is what you get by assuming the strips are centred on their cages - THEY ARE NOT: each strip carries its port numbers at the OUTER end (top strip numbers above the lamps, bottom strip numbers below them), so the strips mirror rather than translate and their tops are 2.9 mm further apart than the cages they serve. The photograph is what broke that tie; it is used here for a pitch, not for an absolute size."},"jack-orientation":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing, read at 8x on the 600 dpi render - the console RJ45 has its latch keyway pointing UP and the OOB RJ45 has it pointing DOWN, so the console is drawn rotate: 180 against std/rj45-ganged (which draws the keyway down). The same check on the SFP+ block: the top-row cages carry their white latch bar at the BOTTOM of the opening and the bottom-row cages carry it at the TOP, so the SFP+ rows ARE mirrored and the lower row is rotate: 180. That is a difference from the sibling S9300-32D, whose provenance records the keyway direction as unresolvable in the images it held; it is resolvable in this device's Figure 11 at 600 dpi and was read there, not borrowed."},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9301-32D end of life end of sale announcement' - no announcement found; the vendor product page, the datasheet PDF and distributor listings (EPS Global) are all live. none-announced is a real finding here, not an absence of looking."},"mgmt-block":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - reset pinhole centred at (9.36, 5.93) with the RESET legend beneath it; a printed white legend block at x 3.0-7.1, y 13.0-25.2 carrying SYS, FAN, PSU0, PSU1 and ID, with the five lamps beside it at x 7.5-11.4 on a uniform 2.58 mm centre pitch (measured centres 13.92 and 24.25 for the first and last; the intermediate readings scattered by up to 0.25 mm and were regularised onto one pitch rather than drawn staggered). A 9.7 x 12.8 mm vent field below. The jack stack top to bottom is console RJ45, USB 3.0 (blue tongue), OOB RJ45 with two integrated green lamps at its lower corners; the legend 'IOIOI (arrows) SS' is printed in one row above the plate and a network symbol below the OOB jack. LED semantics from the HIG section 10 Front Panel LED and Management Port LED tables, transcribed onto each lamp."},"part-numbers":{"note":"The FRU ordering lines are the datasheet's own: PSU-132-AESR / -AISB (1300 W AC, exhaust / intake air flow), PSU-132-DESR / -DISB (1300 W DC) and FAN-405637-HD / -CD (exhaust / intake). NOTE that they are printed here WITHOUT the trailing suffix the library's psu-132-ac contract carries (PSU-132-AISB1); this datasheet prints the shorter form and no held document reconciles the two, so the configurations name no model override and the components keep their own. NO ORDERABLE CHASSIS SKU appears in any held document - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9301-32D - which is recorded as a gap rather than as 'no SKU exists'."},"port-numbers":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the port numerals are printed ON THE BLUE LED STRIPS, not on the panel between the cages, and each interior strip carries TWO of them: the strip between ports 2 and 4 is printed '2' over its left lamp column and '4' over its right. That is what makes the strip-to-port mapping a vendor statement here rather than an inference from adjacency - the left column belongs to the port on its left and the right column to the port on its right, and the two end strips are printed with a single number each ('0'/'1' at the left end, '30'/'31' at the right). Read at 7x on the 600 dpi render. The numbers sit at the OUTER end of each strip and INSIDE its own bezel - measured baselines y 9.5 on the top row and y 37.7 on the bottom. They are drawn here at y 7.2 and 40.0, immediately outside the bezel, because ufispace/qsfpdd-led-strip-2x4@1 carries no text layer and would paint over ink placed where the vendor prints it; the 1.8 mm shift is what keeps them readable and it is a deliberate departure from the measurement, not the measurement. Figure 11 ALSO prints each port's number large and blue on the schematic module face, where a seated module would cover it; those are the figure's annotation and are not modelled."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet 'Typical power: 419 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, which is why power-envelope is bare. The HIG's Connecting Power section states 'The maximum system power consumption is 1246 watts' for both the DC and the AC version, unqualified as to optics or ambient, and that is carried as power-max-w. The two figures come from two documents with two scopes and are NOT reconciled against each other, nor against the sum of the modelled modules. PSU rating is 1300 W per supply (ordering lines); the HIG adds that on a 110 V AC feed each supply delivers only 1000 W and that losing one then leaves the system short."},"qsfp-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - nine LED-strip positions on a measured 45.005 mm group pitch. The seven interior (double-column) strips were measured at centres 114.14, 159.13, 204.23, 249.15, 294.14, 339.24 and 384.17 mm, whose successive differences run 44.92-45.10; the fitted line puts strip k at 69.15 + 45.005k. The two END strips are SINGLE column, and the fit predicts where their single column must fall: 69.15 + 1.4 = 70.55 and 429.19 - 1.4 = 427.79, against 70.47 and 427.90 measured. That agreement is the check that the group pitch is right. Both ends nevertheless SEAT the two-column ufispace/qsfpdd-led-strip-2x4@1, at the notional double-strip position, because the library has no single-column part and none may be built here; the drawn bezel therefore runs 2.8 mm further outboard than the metal at each end, which the matched- scale comparison against the front photograph shows plainly (photo single column at 70.8 and 427.9; the drawn strips span 66.9-71.4 and 426.9-431.5). See the end-led-strip-width gap. Between strips the cage-pair block is 45.005 - 5.6 = 39.405 mm wide (measured 72.1-111.1 for the first block, 38.5 mm mean across all eight), and the two 19.0 mm std/qsfp-dd cages sit in it with even 0.47 mm margins, so cage lefts are 69.15 + 45.005g + 3.27 and + 22.74. Rows: cage tops at y 10.55 and 25.05 per the front-vertical note. The BOTTOM row is drawn rotate: 180 - the vent dashes sit above the top row and below the bottom row with the light cage-to-cage web between them, which is the belly-to-belly pattern. Numbering from Figure 11: top row even 0..30, bottom row odd 1..31, left to right."},"rear-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - HIG rear elevation at 9.658 px/mm (height-derived; see sources). Grounding column at the left edge: two M4 lug holes at x centre 6.26, y 8.02 and 23.80, and the earth symbol below at y 36.0 (HIG section 8 - 'a grounding lug and M4 screws and washers are provided', with two designated locations, one here and one on the side). Six fan bays from x 12.6 on a 51.06 mm pitch, then PSU0 at 319.85 and PSU1 at 378.50 (silver faces measured 319.85-370.35 and 378.50-428.80, i.e. 50.5 and 50.3 against the HIG's stated 50.5 mm PSU width), with the vertical PSU0 and PSU1 legends in the 8.1 mm and 7.2 mm chassis strips after each supply. The fan pitch is the mean of two independent readings of the same repeating feature - the fan status lamps - in two different images: 50.97 mm from the HIG elevation and 51.15 mm from the datasheet rear render. Both lug holes are drawn on a silver ring (4.9 mm outside diameter around the 3.2 mm hole, measured) rather than as bare dark circles: the vendor's collars are bright turned metal, and a dark hole on a dark panel vanished in the first rasterised comparison against the rear photograph."},"sfp-block":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - two silver ganged shells, one per row, measured at x 35.9-64.8 (28.9 mm, against 2 x 14.25 + 0.6 = 29.1 for a two-wide SFP+ ganged block) with a divider at 50.25, so the columns are at x 36.2 and 50.45. The LEFT column is the out-of-band pair: the HIG's 'Connecting the OOB Management Cables' says 'The second port type is the two 10G SFP+ ports also marked with a symbol', and the network symbol is printed over this column. The RIGHT column is the pair under the orange MGMT band, the vendor's ports 0-1: 'Connecting the Management Cables - There are other two 10G SFP+ ports also available for management. These ports are marked with an orange MGMT'. The datasheet calls that pair 1/10G and the HIG port table agrees (rows 0~1, SFP+, 1/10G), while the HIG prose and the Figure 5 callout both say 10G; the group carries 10g and the disagreement is noted here rather than resolved. Each column has FOUR marks above it - an up arrow, two lamps, a down arrow - so one lamp serves the upper port and one the lower, with the arrows saying which is which. Lamp centres measured at 40.3 and 46.2 (OOB column) and 54.25 and 60.25 (MGMT column). The big white '0' and '1' in Figure 11 sit on the highlighted module faces, not on the metal; see the mgmt-port-numerals gap."},"sources":{"note":"UfiSpace S9301-32D datasheet for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9301-32D Hardware Installation Guide (s9301-32d-hig) for the faceplate and rear elevations, the component dimensions table, the LED tables, the grounding and rack-mounting sections; three vendor product renders (photos/s9301-32d-1-view angle, -2-view front, -3-view rear) for colour, counts, construction and one measurement the drawings could not settle. Figure quality was gated before anything was measured: the HIG Port Overview (Figure 11, page 13 of the PDF rendered at 600 dpi) measures 3499 x 348 px across the 436 x 43.8 mm face - aspect 10.055 against a true 9.954, 1.0% out - so it is orthographic enough to carry geometry, and it is the front ruler at 8.025 px/mm. The HIG rear elevation on the same page measures 4158 x 423 px, aspect 9.83, 1.25% out: the HEIGHT is the trusted axis there (9.658 px/mm) because the right-hand edge of the panel is dark on dark and the width detection clipped it. That rescale was checked, not assumed - it moves the measured fan-LED pitch from 51.62 to 50.97 mm, where the datasheet's own rear render (1.95 px/mm, aspect 9.99) independently gives 51.15 mm; before the rescale the two disagreed by 0.9%, after it they agree to 0.4%."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the reading of the cages recorded in this provenance: the 2 SFP pairs (oob-sfp-0/oob-sfp-1 and port-sfp-0/port-sfp-1). Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 16 QSFP-DD pairs (port-0/port-1 to port-30/port-31)."},"vent-islands":{"note":"derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field."},"views":{"note":"Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and the HIG Figure 5 footprint drawing, which prints the fan and PSU handles projecting from the top edge; the three shallow stadium recesses are proportioned off that drawing as FRACTIONS only, because its own aspect is 0.975 against a true 0.676 - it is not to scale along depth at all - so their positions are estimated. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each side carries the five rail attachment pins the HIG rack-mounting section describes ('The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins'), positions estimated on an even 110 mm pitch from 120 mm behind the front face because no drawing dimensions them; the left side near the rear carries the second designated grounding location (HIG Figure 27), its two holes spaced at the 15.8 mm the rear lug holes measure, position estimated. g.data-description: HIG section 10 Front Panel LED table, SYS row - Off (no power), Solid Green (Host CPU/BMC boot complete), Solid Amber (power is up but Host CPU/BMC boot failed)
g.title: led-sys

g.data-description: HIG section 10 Front Panel LED table, FAN row - Off (fans are not initialized), Solid Green (all Fans are work normal), Blinking Amber (fan fail: one or more Fans need service)
g.title: led-fan

g.data-description: HIG section 10 Front Panel LED table, PSU0 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU0 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU0 fail, PSU0 needs service)
g.title: led-psu0

g.data-description: HIG section 10 Front Panel LED table, PSU1 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU1 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU1 fail, PSU1 needs service)
g.title: led-psu1

g.data-description: HIG section 10 Front Panel LED table, ID row - Off (no power), Blinking Blue (beacon feature is enabled on the switch)
g.title: led-id

g.data-description: led-oob-left: HIG section 10 Management Port LED table, Left LED - Off (no power), Solid Green (1G link-up), Blinking Green (1G TX/RX activity); led-oob-right: HIG section 10 Management Port LED table, Right LED - Off (no power), Solid Amber (10M/100M link-up), Blinking Amber (10M/100M TX/RX activity). The two lamps do not share a vocabulary, so they are declared separately
g.title: oob

g.data-description: the left stacked SFP+ pair, marked with the network symbol - the second out-of-band path to the x86 (HIG 'Connecting the OOB Management Cables')
g.title: oob-sfp-0

g.data-description: the left stacked SFP+ pair, marked with the network symbol - the second out-of-band path to the x86 (HIG 'Connecting the OOB Management Cables')
g.title: oob-sfp-1

g.data-description: the right stacked SFP+ pair under the orange MGMT band, the vendor's ports 0-1, usable as Ethernet or in-band management (HIG 'Connecting the Management Cables'; the datasheet and the HIG port table call them 1/10G)
g.title: port-sfp-0

g.data-description: the right stacked SFP+ pair under the orange MGMT band, the vendor's ports 0-1, usable as Ethernet or in-band management (HIG 'Connecting the Management Cables'; the datasheet and the HIG port table call them 1/10G)
g.title: port-sfp-1
